entry.title: Report: America lost over 200,000 media, film, and arts jobs in four years amid AI rise, with movie and sound recording sectors hardest hit [ * ] [ ◻ ]
entry.summary: America has lost more than 200,000 jobs in creative industries over the past four years, including about 50,000 in the last year, marking one of the worst periods for media employment outside major recessions. This decline coincides with the rise of AI systems capable of generating novels, images, music, and other digital art at low cost, though the exact impact of AI on job losses remains difficult to quantify due to factors like industry consolidation and offshoring. Job losses have affected nearly every subsector of digital arts, with the movie and sound recording industry, including Hollywood, losing over 100,000 jobs-about one-third of its workforce-since 2022. Other sectors like publishing and live broadcasting have also seen unusual downturns, while in-person entertainment continues to grow. The ongoing job losses raise questions about the future sustainability of creative industry business models amid advancing AI technologies.

entry.title: Cerebras deploys multi-trillion parameter AI models using multiple WSE-3T wafers with 44 GB on-chip memory each [ * ] [ ◼ ]
entry.summary: Cerebras explains how it deploys large AI models with trillions of parameters by splitting them across multiple WSE-3T wafers, each with 44 GB of on-chip memory, to achieve high throughput of 1000-2000+ tokens per second. The company uses the open source Kimi K3 model with about 3 trillion parameters as an example to illustrate the approach. The deployment involves mapping model layers across 59 wafers, with dense layers assigned one per wafer due to KV cache requirements and linear-attention layers sharing wafers. The wafers are connected in a pipeline where only activations pass between wafers, minimizing data movement. Multiple requests are processed concurrently by keeping the pipeline full, allowing efficient utilization and high throughput.

entry.title: GVS5H method enables five Qwen3.8-27B models to match Fable 5's coding performance on LiveCodeBench hard problems [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
entry.summary: Researchers introduced GVS5H, a ledger-based zero-shot self-orchestration method that allows multiple instances of a single model to decompose and coordinate on coding problems through a shared filesystem. Using this approach, five Qwen3.8-27B models achieved up to 92.4% pass@1 accuracy on the 100 latest hard LiveCodeBench problems, matching or exceeding Fable 5's 90.4% at a fraction of the cost. The method was tested across eleven open and closed-weight models, showing gains of up to 25.6 percentage points on pinned backends. The improvement is attributed to problem decomposition and persistent context management during inference, enabling frontier-level coding accuracy without additional training. The code and results are available under open licenses on GitHub.

entry.title: Researchers find AI-generated text uses more complex linguistic features than human writing, potentially reducing readability due to optimization for information density over communication [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
entry.summary: A study analyzing AI-generated text across various domains found that language models frequently use psycholinguistic features associated with human processing difficulty, such as long syntactic dependencies and low-frequency word combinations. Compared to human writing and paraphrases, AI models tend to employ more inanimate subjects with animate verbs and other complex structures, which may make their output harder to understand. The researchers suggest this arises because AI models optimize for goals like math and reasoning that prioritize information density rather than clear communication. They demonstrated this by fine-tuning a model with a length penalty, which increased divergence from human-like language patterns. The findings highlight misalignments between human linguistic processing and AI-generated language, pointing to potential avenues for improving AI text clarity.

entry.title: EPFL develops LogSync neural chip to decode cross-regional brain interactions and identify cognitive and emotional states in real time for psychiatric therapy [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
entry.summary: EPFL researchers have created an implantable neural chip called LogSync that records brain activity across multiple regions to detect cognitive and emotional states in real time. The chip uses low power and machine-learning algorithms to analyze brain wave synchrony and generate stimulation triggers, aiming to improve treatments for psychiatric disorders such as depression and PTSD. LogSync was tested on human brain recordings and animal models, demonstrating its ability to track brain oscillations and trigger stimulation at precise phases. The system operates under 200 microwatts of power by combining hardware and algorithm design, using logarithmic computations to efficiently process neural signals. This technology could enhance adaptive deep brain stimulation and other neurotechnologies beyond psychiatric applications.

entry.title: Red5 plans AI detection service with real-time frame extraction to enhance live streaming analytics and content moderation [ * ] [ ◼ ]
entry.summary: Red5 is developing an AI detection service that enables real-time extraction of video frames from live streams across various protocols, allowing for instant AI analysis and enhanced live streaming capabilities. This technology supports both conventional HTTP streaming and Red5's Cloud Experience Delivery Network (XDN) infrastructure, enabling applications such as content moderation, surveillance, sports highlights, and quality control with minimal latency. The service can extract frames at sub-second intervals and push them to cloud storage for immediate AI processing, often completing analysis before the primary content reaches viewers. This advancement aims to overcome previous delays in frame extraction and unlock new use cases by combining hardware-accelerated cloud processing with Red5's streaming platform architecture.

entry.summary: OpenAI has secured significant AI business from major customers like Rippling, Replit, and DataCamp by offering discounts of up to 90%, leading these companies to shift their AI workloads away from Anthropic. This aggressive pricing strategy has contributed to a slowdown in Anthropic's growth and reflects OpenAI's focus on expanding market share despite reduced margins. The discounts include a 30% price cut on a $100 million contract with Replit and an 80 to 90% cost reduction for DataCamp. OpenAI has also doubled ChatGPT seats for a US bank at a substantially lower per-user price. These price reductions are supported by OpenAI's more efficient Sol and Luna model lines. Both OpenAI and Anthropic face increasing price pressure from Chinese AI providers offering competitive models at lower costs.

entry.title: Researchers release OpenMobile-2, an open-source AI smartphone agent trained on 110+ simulated apps, achieving top performance among open models on real Android devices [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
entry.summary: Researchers from Nanjing University, SenseTime, and other institutions developed OpenMobile-2, an open-source AI smartphone agent trained on over 110 simulated applications, including replicas of popular apps like Taobao and Slack. The agent was tested on real Android devices and achieved the highest score among open-source models on the SPA-Bench benchmark, demonstrating that open-source smartphone agents can rival proprietary ones. The team rebuilt apps to create a controlled training environment that avoids challenges of using real apps, such as login requirements and state persistence. They found that increasing the diversity of apps in training improved the agent's success rate on unseen applications more than simply increasing data volume. OpenMobile-2 models, built on Qwen3.5 and Qwen3.6 architectures, showed significant performance gains on multiple benchmarks, with the larger model scoring 59.6 points on SPA-Bench, nearly doubling previous open-source results. The researchers also experimented with direct command interfaces in simulated apps, allowing the agent to bypass menu navigation, which improved task completion rates when the agent was trained to use these shortcuts. While reinforcement learning added limited benefits, the overall results suggest that open-source AI agents can effectively operate smartphone apps and approach the capabilities of proprietary models.

entry.title: Anthropic open-sources Claude Code's sandbox-runtime as Apache-2.0 npm package with macOS, Linux, and Windows support [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
entry.summary: Anthropic has released the sandbox-runtime (srt) used in Claude Code as an open-source npm package under the Apache-2.0 license. The runtime provides OS-level sandboxing for filesystem and network restrictions without requiring containers, supporting macOS, Linux, and Windows platforms. The sandbox-runtime uses native primitives like sandbox-exec with Seatbelt profiles on macOS, bubblewrap on Linux, and a Windows build combining Windows Filtering Platform filters and NTFS ACLs. Features include allow-only network policies, Unix-socket allowlisting, experimental TLS termination, credential masking, and AWS SigV4 signing. The release is framed as a research preview for safer AI agents, with evolving APIs and some Windows limitations noted.

entry.title: Zephium launches an open-source browser and integrated work environment with AI agent collaboration and native ad blocking on WebKit and WebView2 engines [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
entry.summary: Zephium has released an open-source browser built in Rust that uses the native WebKit engine on macOS and WebView2 on Windows, offering native ad and tracker blocking, Chrome extension support, and a unique integrated work environment called Work. Work allows users to describe outcomes in natural language and watch AI agents perform tasks in parallel on a canvas, with results and plans laid out visually and linked to task management tools. The browser features a sidebar assistant called Ask Zephium that reads and interacts with web pages, and supports multiple AI models through user-provided keys or Zephium AI's own selection. Zephium emphasizes privacy with no telemetry and local storage of history and tasks, and includes features like vertical tabs, customizable shortcuts, and importing from other browsers. Work integrates with various services and command-line tools, enabling users to manage complex workflows without leaving the browser.
